summary: Resubmitted update.json with two additions from this turn's source work, no receipts touched. First, the trigger now has a code anchor for the value it depends on: tryStageCommitIndex (raft.go 1392-1404) stages the commit index into the store only when RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore, and InmemCommitTrackingStore declares that interface (inmem_store.go:12) — which is the code-level reason a cluster that never ran with the flag carries a staged value of zero while one that has run with it carries the commit index, exactly the contrast the latent-trap receipts measure (656e33fb90f24c58a94928eeeeb938aa and 202311f4911e4af5828d49134f37811c). That anchor is registered as a source (25 declared sources now) and attached to the primary investigation and interpretation. Second, the scoped negative on documentation is widened from the named markdown files to the whole captured tree: a recursive search for RestoreCommittedLogs and CommitTrackingLogStore across all 91 captured files returns only six Go files (api.go, config.go, inmem_store.go, log.go, raft.go, raft_test.go) and no non-Go surface, so README.md, docs/README.md, docs/apply.md, docs/divergence.md, membership.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, fuzzy/readme.md, the .github templates and workflows, the Makefile and the module files say nothing about the feature; the negative remains scoped to the captured tree, not to upstream releases. Conclusions, comparisons, counterevidence and the previously recorded limitations — including the earlier source-anchor audit and the two known blemishes — are unchanged, and the finding still stands as validated: the trigger is the persisted commit index at or above the newest configuration entry, with the empty-configuration, stale-membership, resurrected-voter, forgotten-added-voter, client-contract and operator-recovery consequences each receipt-backed with controls and repeats.
